finding: Dialog correctly uses native <dialog> element with role="alertdialog" variant support, aria-labelledby wired to heading ID, aria-describedby wired to description element, and aria-modal="true" for modal variant.

Focus trap is implemented with Tab/Shift+Tab wrapping across shadow boundary, Escape fires hx-cancel and closes dialog, initial focus moves to first focusable element on open, and focus restores to trigger element on close per WCAG 2.4.3.

Focus delegation works correctly for light DOM content. The fallback when no light DOM focusable elements exist correctly uses the shadow close button. However, delegatesFocus is not set on shadowRootOptions, so tab order for the shadow close button relies entirely on the manual focus trap rather than native delegation.
recommendation: Consider adding `static override shadowRootOptions = { ...LitElement.shadowRootOptions, delegatesFocus: true }` as a secondary safety net, though the manual trap is currently adequate.

finding: Dialog heading rendered as <h2> with stable ID referenced by aria-labelledby. Description property renders visually-hidden span with stable ID referenced by aria-describedby. Fallback aria-label applied when no heading or header slot.

Combobox correctly implements ARIA 1.2 pattern with role="combobox" on the input, aria-expanded, aria-autocomplete="list", aria-controls pointing to listbox, aria-activedescendant tracking focused option, and aria-labelledby wired to the label element.

Arrow keys navigate options, Enter selects, Escape closes and clears, Tab closes naturally, Home/End jump to first/last enabled option. Disabled options are skipped. Multi-select chip remove buttons have accessible aria-label via labelRemoveOption callback.
Filter results are announced via a dedicated polite live region with aria-atomic="true" that announces option count on each keystroke. The error slot uses role="alert" for error announcements.

Label association uses for/id pattern within the same shadow root, which is correct. However when ariaLabel overrides the label property, aria-labelledby is omitted but aria-label is set, which is correct. The help text id is included in aria-describedby only when helpText property is set, not when the help-text slot is populated.
recommendation: Extend describedBy computation to also include _helpTextId when the help-text slot has assigned nodes, so slotted help text is programmatically associated via aria-describedby.

finding: The combobox trigger is a <div> with role="combobox" rather than a native <input> or <button>. This is the documented APG pattern for custom selects and is acceptable, but JAWS older versions handle div-combobox inconsistently. The hidden native <select> correctly has aria-hidden="true" and tabindex="-1".
recommendation: Add a brief comment in the source citing the APG reference for div combobox so future maintainers do not incorrectly revert to a <button> which would break the combobox semantics.

finding: Arrow keys navigate options, Enter/Space open and select, Escape closes and focuses trigger, Tab closes naturally, Home/End navigate to first/last, and single-character typeahead jumps to matching option. All patterns follow ARIA APG combobox with listbox.

hx-select has no live region to announce the number of available options when the listbox opens or when options are filtered. Screen reader users have no way to know how many options are available without navigating through them.
recommendation: Add a visually-hidden polite aria-live region that announces option count when the listbox opens, matching the pattern in hx-combobox (_filterAnnouncement).

finding: Label uses for/id pattern within shadow root. aria-describedby correctly wired to error and help text IDs. aria-required and aria-invalid applied conditionally with `nothing` to omit when not applicable.

Native <input type="range"> is used, which natively carries role="slider" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax. aria-valuetext is exposed via the valueText property for human-readable alternatives. The visual thumb overlay is aria-hidden.

Label rendered as <label for="{sliderId}"> within shadow root ensuring native label association. aria-labelledby references label ID, aria-describedby references help text ID. devWarn fires when no label is provided at WCAG 4.1.2 violation level.

Native range input handles all keyboard interactions: Arrow keys increment/decrement by step, Home jumps to min, End jumps to max. No custom keyboard handler needed; native semantics cover WCAG 2.1.1.

Uses semantic <fieldset> with <legend> for group labeling. role="radiogroup" is applied to the fieldset even though fieldset implicitly has that role — this is redundant but not harmful. aria-describedby correctly references both error and help text wrapper IDs.
recommendation: Remove the redundant role="radiogroup" from the <fieldset> element since fieldset inherently maps to radiogroup in the accessibility tree when it contains radio inputs.

finding: Roving tabindex is correctly implemented across hx-radio children. Arrow keys move selection and focus simultaneously per ARIA APG radio group pattern. Space selects focused radio. Home/End keys implemented. Arrow wrapping is correct (circular).

Error wrapper div always rendered with stable _errorId so aria-describedby remains valid even before an error appears. WCAG 1.3.1 wrapper pattern is correct. devWarn fires when no label or aria-label is provided.

Tabs use role="tablist" with aria-orientation and aria-label. Tab panels use aria-label (derived from tab text content) instead of aria-labelledby to avoid shadow DOM boundary failures — this is the correct workaround. However, the fallback `aria-labelledby` used when tab text is not yet available can fail across shadow boundaries.
recommendation: In _syncTabsAndPanels, ensure the tabLabel fallback path is reliably resolved after slotchange; consider adding a MutationObserver or slotchange listener on hx-tab to re-run panel labeling once content is available.

finding: Arrow keys navigate tabs, Enter/Space activate in manual or automatic mode respectively, Home/End jump to first/last tab. Disabled tabs receive focus but are not activated per APG. The tablist correctly handles both orientations.

Tab focus management is partially split between the hx-tab host element tabindex and the inner shadow button. Focusing `targetTab.shadowRoot?.querySelector('button')?.focus()` directly pierces shadow DOM, which can be fragile if the internal structure of hx-tab changes. Additionally when the default label is 'Tabs', it's uninformative for AT users.
recommendation: Expose a focus() method on hx-tab that delegates internally; use that instead of direct shadowRoot querySelector. Require a non-default `label` attribute at component validation time.

finding: Uses <header> landmark containing <nav> with aria-label. Mobile toggle button has aria-expanded, aria-controls referencing nav-menu div, and contextual aria-label that updates between 'Open navigation' and 'Close navigation'.

Escape key closes mobile menu and returns focus to toggle button. However, the nav items inside the slot (provided by consumers) are expected to handle their own keyboard navigation. The component does not enforce or validate keyboard patterns on slotted nav items.
recommendation: Document in JSDoc that consumers are responsible for ensuring slotted nav items are keyboard navigable (e.g., using hx-nav-item). Add a devWarn if slotted content contains non-interactive elements with no tabindex.

finding: Uses native <button> with role="switch" and aria-checked correctly toggling between 'true' and 'false'. aria-labelledby references the label element ID. aria-describedby references error or help text IDs. aria-invalid applied when error is present.
Space key toggles the switch per ARIA APG switch pattern. The native button element handles Enter as well. Keyboard handler only intercepts Space to prevent page scroll, which is correct.

Label association uses aria-labelledby from button to label element within the same shadow root. The <label> has `for` referencing the button ID, but `for` does not associate labels with buttons in the HTML-AAM spec — only aria-labelledby provides the association here.
recommendation: The aria-labelledby is correct and sufficient. The `for` attribute on the label pointing to the button ID is technically incorrect (for only works with labelable elements, not buttons) but is harmless and should be changed to avoid future confusion — remove the `for` attribute from the label or add a comment explaining the aria-labelledby is the operative association.

finding: Native <input type="number"> is used correctly. Stepper buttons have tabindex="-1" to keep them out of tab order (intended for mouse/pointer use only). aria-invalid and aria-describedby are applied. Increment/decrement labels are configurable via incrementLabel/decrementLabel properties.
recommendation: Consider adding aria-live announcement when stepper buttons change the value so screen reader users who activate steppers via mouse/assistive pointer can hear the new value without moving focus to the input.

finding: Arrow Up/Down keys increment/decrement the value when the input is focused. The native input also handles Page Up/Down for large steps. Stepper buttons are intentionally removed from tab order (tabindex=-1) since the arrow keys provide equivalent keyboard access.

Label association uses native <label for="{inputId}"> within shadow root. Slotted label is assigned an ID and referenced via aria-labelledby. Error and help text IDs are conditionally included in aria-describedby. Required marker is aria-hidden.

Uses native <input type="checkbox"> with aria-checked="mixed" for indeterminate state, aria-invalid for error state, aria-describedby for error/help text association. The mixinDelegatesAria mixin correctly handles aria-label forwarding.

Error announcement uses role="status" (implicit aria-live="polite") with a deferred _announcedError that clears and re-populates via rAF to re-trigger AT announcement on value change. This is a sophisticated and correct pattern for WCAG 4.1.3.
recommendation: Document the deliberate use of role="status" over role="alert" in a code comment since status is less commonly used for error patterns and may surprise future maintainers.

finding: @media (forced-colors: active) block exists in styles and sets forced-color-adjust patterns for the checkbox box and checkmark. However the SVG checkmark stroke in forced-colors may not have sufficient contrast since currentColor resolves to system text color which may conflict with the forced Highlight background.
recommendation: In the forced-colors block, set the SVG checkmark stroke to HighlightText explicitly: `.checkbox__icon { stroke: HighlightText; }` when the checkbox is in checked state.

finding: Error summary uses role="alert" with aria-atomic="true" for full re-announcement. Focus is programmatically moved to the error summary on failed submission via tabindex="-1", meeting WCAG 2.4.3. setErrors() applies aria-invalid to named fields.

The hx-form component is Light DOM (createRenderRoot returns this) which is correct for Drupal compatibility, but the getFormElements() selector list is hardcoded and does not include hx-number-input, hx-date-picker, hx-combobox, hx-time-picker, or hx-slider. These components will not receive aria-invalid from setErrors().
recommendation: Expand the hx-form getFormElements() selector to include all form-associated hx-* components: add 'hx-number-input, hx-date-picker, hx-combobox, hx-time-picker, hx-slider' to the querySelectorAll argument.

finding: Carousel uses role="region" with aria-label and aria-roledescription="carousel". Navigation buttons have accessible labels. Pagination dots have aria-label and aria-current. However the component has TWO concurrent live regions: a manual live-region div (aria-live toggled off/polite) AND the slide-viewport also has aria-live="polite" with aria-atomic="false" — this creates potential double announcements.
recommendation: Remove aria-live="polite" from the slide-viewport element. Use only the dedicated live-region div to announce slide changes, toggling it from 'off' to 'polite' on navigation. This prevents double-announcement in JAWS and NVDA.

finding: Arrow Left/Right (horizontal) and Up/Down (vertical) navigate slides. Home/End jump to first/last. However, the carousel container is not explicitly focusable (no tabindex on the base element) so keyboard navigation via arrow keys may not be reachable by keyboard users who cannot click to focus the container first.
recommendation: Add tabindex="0" to the base div or the slide-viewport so keyboard users can tab into the carousel and then use arrow keys. Fire _handleKeydown on the focused element.

finding: Alert sets role="alert" or role="status" on the host element based on variant, correctly applying assertive vs polite announcement. A visually-hidden sr-only div with explicit aria-live provides announcements for JAWS+Chrome and NVDA which do not re-announce when aria-hidden is merely removed. The severity label is always rendered visually-hidden so color alone does not convey information.

The dismissible close button correctly removes the alert from the DOM flow. returnFocusTo property allows focus to be restored to a specified element after dismissal. However, if returnFocusTo is not set, focus is lost when the alert closes — the component dispatches hx-after-close but the consumer must manage focus.
recommendation: Document prominently in JSDoc and Storybook that returnFocusTo must be set when the dismiss action is the primary interactive element, to satisfy WCAG 2.4.3. Consider defaulting to returning focus to document.body as a safe fallback.

finding: Calendar popup uses role="dialog" with aria-modal and aria-label. The text input has aria-haspopup="dialog" and the trigger button has aria-expanded and aria-controls. Day buttons have accessible labels. However the read-only text input also has aria-haspopup="dialog" which may confuse some AT — typically aria-haspopup on the button trigger is sufficient.
recommendation: Remove aria-haspopup="dialog" from the readonly text input; keep it only on the trigger button (the calendar icon button). Screen readers should only announce the popup affordance once.

finding: Calendar keyboard navigation (arrow keys within grid, Escape to close, Enter to select) is implemented. However, the calendar popup element itself does not receive focus when opened — focus handling inside the calendar grid must be audited to confirm keyboard users can reach day buttons without first tabbing through all navigation buttons.
recommendation: Ensure that when the calendar opens, focus is explicitly moved to the currently selected day button (or today's date if none selected), not just to the calendar container element.

finding: Comprehensive forced-colors block present in styles: ButtonText for input borders, Highlight for focus outlines, HighlightText for selected day text, LinkText for today indicator border and error states, GrayText for disabled days. Today dot indicator hidden in forced-colors (correct, border takes over).

Month navigation announces the new month name via a visually-hidden live region (_liveMessage). This correctly informs screen reader users when the calendar month changes without requiring them to re-read the entire calendar grid.

Menu uses role="menu" with aria-label. Menu items use role="menuitem" (on hx-menu-item children). Escape dispatches hx-close event. Typeahead buffer accumulation is implemented for keyboard navigation. devWarn fires when label is missing.

ArrowDown/Up navigate between items, Home/End jump to first/last, Escape closes, typeahead jumps to first matching item. Roving tabindex is synchronized across items. All patterns follow ARIA APG menu pattern.

Drawer uses role="dialog" with aria-modal="true". aria-labelledby priority chain is correctly implemented: slot-based labelledby takes precedence over aria-label prop which falls back to 'Drawer'. Background elements receive aria-hidden="true" when drawer is open to hide inert content from AT.

Focus is trapped within the drawer with Tab/Shift+Tab wrapping. Initial focus fires hx-initial-focus (cancelable) to allow override. Focus is restored to trigger element on close per WCAG 2.4.3. hx-initial-focus event allows consumers to customize initial focus target for clinical workflows.

Uses native <button> element for button variant and <a> for link variant. aria-busy is set during loading state. aria-disabled is applied for disabled anchor variant since anchors have no native disabled. Loading state suppresses click and removes href. devWarn fires when no accessible name is present.

Button variant correctly avoids aria-disabled on native button (native disabled attribute is the correct mechanism). Anchor variant correctly uses aria-disabled plus tabindex="-1" since anchors lack native disabled. This dual-branch approach is correct per ARIA spec.

Native <input> with aria-invalid, aria-describedby referencing error and help text IDs, and aria-labelledby/aria-label for accessible naming. Error announced via role="alert" with aria-atomic. Required uses native attribute (HTML-AAM implicit aria-required mapping).

Label association handles three scenarios: label property (for/id in shadow root), label slot (slotted label gets ID for aria-labelledby), and aria-label attribute override. All paths correctly associate the input with its accessible name.

Breadcrumb uses <nav aria-label> landmark with an ordered list. The label defaults to 'Breadcrumb' and is configurable. The current page item should be marked aria-current="page" on the last breadcrumb-item — need to verify hx-breadcrumb-item implementation for this.
recommendation: Verify hx-breadcrumb-item sets aria-current="page" on the final item automatically or that consumers are required to set it.

finding: hx-accordion-item uses <details>/<summary> with role="heading" aria-level on the <summary>. While this approach avoids the aria-expanded/aria-controls pattern, using role="heading" on <summary> overrides the native summary disclosure semantics. The APG accordion pattern expects role="button" inside a heading, not role="heading" on the trigger itself.
recommendation: Restructure to use the standard APG accordion pattern: a <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls inside an element with role="heading" aria-level="N", rather than role="heading" on the <summary> element.

finding: hx-accordion manages ArrowUp/ArrowDown between items at the container level. However, since items use <details>/<summary>, the native Enter key handles toggle. Space activation is not explicitly handled in the summary — browsers treat Space on summary as click which works but is not guaranteed across all AT.
recommendation: Add explicit Space key handler in hx-accordion-item to prevent default and programmatically toggle, ensuring consistent behavior across NVDA+Firefox and JAWS+Chrome combinations.

finding: Tooltip correctly injects a visually-hidden element into the document root (not shadow root) to work around aria-describedby shadow DOM boundary limitation. The trigger element's aria-describedby is set to this document-level element ID. However, if multiple tooltips exist simultaneously, the injected element cleanup must be reliable to prevent ID collisions.
recommendation: Verify that the document-level tooltip element is cleaned up in disconnectedCallback and that the ID includes the component's stable unique ID (not just a generic counter) to prevent collisions when components are dynamically added/removed.

finding: Popover sets aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded on the anchor element. Focus trap with Tab/Shift+Tab is implemented. Escape restores focus to the prior element. For non-interactive popovers, focus is intentionally not stolen per the comment citing WCAG 2.4.3.

Table uses role="grid" with aria-label and aria-busy. Sortable column headers use aria-sort. Row selection uses aria-selected. The roving tabindex pattern is implemented for sortable headers. However, the loading skeleton row has aria-hidden="true" but the table body still announces via role="grid" during loading.
recommendation: When loading=true, verify that the empty/loading state cells do not receive focus and are fully excluded from AT interaction via aria-disabled or inert on the tbody.

finding: ArrowLeft/Right keyboard navigation is implemented for sortable column headers. Row click dispatches hx-row-click. However, there is no keyboard activation for row click (Enter/Space on a data row should fire hx-row-click for keyboard users when rows are intended to be interactive).
recommendation: If rows are interactive (have hx-row-click listeners), add role="row" with tabindex and Enter/Space key handlers on the <tr> elements to make row activation keyboard accessible.

finding: Side navigation uses <nav aria-label> landmark with roving tabindex for nested hx-nav-item children. The collapse toggle has aria-expanded and aria-label ('Expand navigation'/'Collapse navigation'). Collapsed state is reflected via the host attribute for CSS targeting.

Dropzone uses role="button" with tabindex, aria-label, and aria-labelledby correctly applied. File list uses <ul> with aria-label. Remove buttons have contextual aria-labels with file names. Upload progress bars use role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max and descriptive aria-label.
recommendation: The dropzone uses div role="button" rather than a native <button>. Consider using a native <button> with type="button" to get keyboard activation for free and improve AT compatibility, particularly on Android TalkBack where div role="button" activation can be inconsistent.

finding: Time picker uses role="combobox" on the input with aria-expanded, aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-controls, and aria-autocomplete. The aria-labelledby cross-root linking requires assigning an ID to the slotted label element (A-03 workaround) — this is correctly implemented. However aria-describedby referencing error/help IDs in shadow DOM from a shadow element is within the same root so is valid.

PHI field masks sensitive data with aria-label that toggles between reveal/hide actions. The toggle button uses aria-pressed to communicate current state. A polite aria-live region announces the mask/reveal action. Masked content is replaced with aria-hidden decorative characters.

Patient banner sets aria-label on the host element for the patient's name context. An assertive alert region is used for critical clinical alerts. However, aria-invalid is set on the host element in some states, which may confuse AT since the host is not a form control.
recommendation: Remove aria-invalid from the host element. aria-invalid should only be applied to form control elements. For clinical alert states, use a dedicated role="alert" region inside the shadow DOM instead of mutating the host's ARIA state.

finding: Dual-mode implementation: precision=1 uses role="radiogroup" with radio stars and aria-checked; precision=0.5 uses role="slider" with aria-valuemin/max/now/text to avoid label-content-name mismatch; readonly uses role="img" with descriptive aria-label. This is a sophisticated and correct ARIA implementation.

The 2D saturation/value gradient picker uses role="slider" with a single aria-valuenow (saturation only) and aria-valuetext announcing both axes. The documented limitation (WCAG 4.1.2 note) is acknowledged in the code. However, a two-dimensional control fundamentally cannot be represented by a single slider, leaving value-axis navigation inaccessible to AT users.
recommendation: Consider providing an alternative numeric input fields for saturation and value (HSV) as keyboard-accessible alternatives to the 2D gradient picker. These could be visually collapsed but available to keyboard/AT users, ensuring the full range of color selection is accessible.

finding: Pagination uses <nav> landmark with aria-label. A polite aria-live region announces the current page on navigation. Roving tabindex manages focus between page buttons. First/Previous/Next/Last buttons have descriptive aria-labels. aria-disabled is used on the current page button rather than native disabled to keep it in tab order.

Toast correctly applies role="alert" or role="status" based on variant. aria-live and aria-atomic are set. aria-hidden is managed when toast is not open. Close button has aria-label. Pattern mirrors hx-alert's approach to avoid double-announcement in JAWS.

Meter uses role="meter" (not progressbar) with aria-valuenow/min/max and aria-valuetext that includes the state label. tabindex="0" makes it keyboard focusable. The visual track has aria-hidden="true". aria-labelledby correctly references the visible label element.

Progress bar uses role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max/text. For indeterminate state, aria-valuenow is omitted (undefined). A polite aria-live region announces progress completion. The variant label is embedded in aria-valuetext so color is not the sole conveyor of state.

Spinner has two modes: decorative (role="presentation", no aria-label) and meaningful (role="status", aria-label). Guards against empty aria-label string which would be a WCAG failure. The JSDoc documents the companion aria-busy pattern for containers.

Icon button requires aria-label (enforced and normalized). For anchor variant: aria-disabled plus tabindex="-1" is correctly applied for disabled state since anchors lack native disabled. For button variant: aria-disabled is intentionally omitted (native disabled is sufficient). SVG icon is aria-hidden.

Toggle button uses native <button> with aria-pressed toggling between 'true' and 'false'. aria-label is supported for icon-only variants. The pressed state is communicated via aria-pressed, not only by visual means, satisfying WCAG 1.4.1 for state.

Split button correctly splits the primary action button and the dropdown trigger. Dropdown trigger has aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded, and aria-controls. The dropdown menu has role="menu" with aria-label. Both buttons have accessible labels.

Dot badges use role="img" with aria-label when dotLabel is provided. Count badges use aria-live="polite" to announce count changes. Remove button has aria-label. However, dot badges without dotLabel have neither role nor aria-label, making them invisible to AT.
recommendation: When dotLabel is not provided, add aria-hidden="true" to the badge so AT users are not exposed to an unlabeled decorative element.

finding: Tag remove button has aria-label="Remove {tag label}". The tag component notes that aria-live announcements for removal are the consumer's responsibility. However, no guidance exists in the JSDoc for how consumers should implement the announcement.
recommendation: Add JSDoc example showing how the consuming page should implement an aria-live region that announces filter/tag removal to meet WCAG 4.1.3. The component-level note is insufficient without actionable guidance.

finding: Steps uses role="list" with aria-label. devWarn fires when aria-label is missing. The component notes this in JSDoc. However, individual step items need to communicate current step, completed steps, and upcoming steps to AT — the aria-label of each step item needs verification.
recommendation: Verify hx-step-item exposes aria-current="step" on the active item and visual state (completed/upcoming) is communicated via aria-label or aria-describedby, not solely through visual indicators.

finding: Tree view implements role="tree" with role="treeitem" on items per WAI-ARIA tree pattern. Roving tabindex is implemented. aria-label required on the container. Expandable items use aria-expanded.

Overflow menu uses a trigger button with aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded, and aria-controls (conditionally when open). The inner panel has role="menu" with aria-label. The design correctly omits aria-controls when the menu is closed to avoid referencing a non-existent ID.

The card has delegatesFocus enabled via shadowRootOptions. Interactive cards (hx-href) should use an anchor element or button rather than a div with role and tabindex for link semantics. The heading slot note correctly requires consumers to use semantic heading elements. The ARIA anti-pattern warning for actions+href combination is documented.
recommendation: Verify the hx-card implementation for interactive (hx-href) mode uses role="link" with tabindex and appropriate keyboard activation (Enter key), and confirm consumers receive a dev warning when both hx-href and actions slot are populated simultaneously.

finding: Disabled links correctly use role="link" with aria-disabled="true" and tabindex="0" to keep them in tab order but communicate their disabled state. Active links use native <a> elements. This is the correct pattern for disabled link semantics.

forced-colors media query support is inconsistent across the component library. hx-date-picker, hx-checkbox, hx-tag, hx-help-text have it; the majority of components (hx-button, hx-select, hx-combobox, hx-slider, hx-radio-group, hx-switch, hx-number-input, hx-tabs, hx-dialog, hx-drawer, hx-carousel, hx-accordion, hx-alert, hx-toast, hx-spinner, hx-breadcrumb, hx-side-nav, hx-top-nav) are missing it entirely.
recommendation: Conduct a library-wide forced-colors audit. At minimum each interactive component must: (1) use outline instead of box-shadow for focus rings (box-shadow is ignored in forced-colors), (2) use ButtonText/HighlightText system colors for borders and text, and (3) not rely solely on background-color to communicate state (checked, selected, active, error).

finding: Multiple components use box-shadow for focus rings (hx-combobox, hx-slider, hx-select, hx-number-input, hx-time-picker). box-shadow is invisible in Windows High Contrast Mode (forced-colors). Components that rely solely on box-shadow for focus indication will have zero visible focus indicator in forced-colors mode, violating WCAG 2.4.7.
recommendation: Replace box-shadow focus indicators with outline: 2px solid var(--hx-focus-ring-color) with outline-offset. Where box-shadow is used for the aesthetic glow, add a transparent outline as a fallback, and in the forced-colors block set outline: 2px solid Highlight. See hx-date-picker styles for the correct pattern.

finding: Color tokens use design system values (primary-500 = #2563eb on neutral-0 = #ffffff yields approximately 8.6:1 contrast ratio — passes AA). Error red (error-500 = #dc3545 on white) yields approximately 5.9:1 — passes AA. Neutral-400 placeholder text (#adb5bd on white) yields approximately 2.9:1 — FAILS WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for normal text.
recommendation: Increase placeholder text token from neutral-400 (#adb5bd) to at minimum neutral-500 (#6c757d) which yields approximately 4.6:1 contrast ratio on white. Update all components that use --hx-color-neutral-400 for placeholder text.

finding: The library consistently uses `nothing` from Lit to omit ARIA attributes when not applicable (rather than empty strings or 'false'), which is correct per the ARIA spec. However, several components apply aria-required="true" to native form elements which already communicate required via the native required attribute — this creates redundant but not harmful duplication.
recommendation: For native form elements (input, select, textarea), prefer the native `required` attribute alone. Per HTML-AAM, required maps implicitly to aria-required. Remove explicit aria-required from native inputs to avoid redundancy and keep the pattern consistent.

finding: hx-alert and hx-toast correctly implement a two-phase live region strategy (sr-only div for AT + host role for semantic). hx-select lacks a live region for filter/option count announcements. Several dynamic widgets (hx-combobox, hx-select) have inconsistent live region patterns — hx-combobox has one, hx-select does not.
recommendation: Standardize the live region pattern: every selection widget that filters or changes option availability must have a polite live region announcing option count. Apply the hx-combobox _filterAnnouncement pattern to hx-select.

finding: Using role="heading" directly on a <summary> element creates a conflict: the native <summary> element has an implicit role of 'button', and applying role="heading" overrides it without providing a button child. Screen readers may announce the accordion trigger as a heading without any button affordance, making activation non-obvious in browse mode.
recommendation: Refactor hx-accordion-item to use the standard APG accordion pattern: an element with role="heading" aria-level containing a <button aria-expanded aria-controls>. Remove the <details>/<summary> elements and manage open/close state manually.

finding: The 2D gradient picker provides only arrow key navigation for the focused axis (horizontal saturation only). The value (brightness) axis is not reachable via keyboard when using the gradient control. This means keyboard-only users cannot select a full range of colors, making the gradient interaction partially inaccessible.
recommendation: Add Shift+ArrowUp/Down or a secondary axis navigation pattern for the value (brightness) dimension, OR provide visible numeric input fields for HSV/HSL/RGB values as required keyboard alternatives to the 2D gradient control.

finding: The dropzone uses div role="button" with tabindex rather than a native <button> element. On Android TalkBack and some JAWS configurations, div role="button" elements may not receive Enter key activation consistently. Additionally, the hidden native <input type="file"> inside the dropzone is activated via click() calls which may not work in all AT contexts.
recommendation: Replace the dropzone div role="button" with a native <button type="button"> wrapping the dropzone content. The native file input can remain hidden with visual-only styling but should be reliably triggered from the button.

finding: The carousel has two concurrent aria-live regions: (1) a dedicated live-region div that toggles between aria-live="off" and aria-live="polite" on manual navigation, and (2) the slide-viewport div that permanently has aria-live="polite" with aria-atomic="false". When slides change, both regions may announce causing double announcements in NVDA and JAWS, which is a significant usability issue for screen reader users.
recommendation: Remove aria-live="polite" from the slide-viewport element entirely. Rely solely on the dedicated live-region div with controlled aria-live toggling. Set aria-live to 'polite' briefly during navigation then reset to 'off' after the announcement fires.

finding: SUMMARY WCAG 2.1 AA COMPLIANCE VERDICT: The HELiX component library demonstrates strong foundational accessibility with correct ARIA patterns in the majority of components, consistent use of ElementInternals for form association, native HTML elements preferred over custom ARIA roles in most cases, and devWarn guidance for missing accessible names. Critical issues requiring remediation before 3.0.0 release: (1) Inconsistent forced-colors support across ~80% of components — box-shadow focus rings are invisible in Windows High Contrast Mode; (2) hx-accordion uses role=heading on <summary> conflicting with native disclosure button semantics; (3) hx-color-picker 2D gradient is inaccessible to keyboard-only users; (4) hx-carousel double live-region causes screen reader double-announcement; (5) hx-file-upload div role=button is unreliable in TalkBack; (6) hx-select lacks option count live region; (7) Placeholder text color token (#adb5bd) fails WCAG 1.4.3 contrast at 2.9:1. High-severity issues: 4. Medium-severity issues: 5. Low-severity issues: 14. Pass: remainder. Overall readiness score: 7/10 — not ready for 3.0.0 release without remediation of critical issues.
recommendation: Address in priority order: (1) Add forced-colors @media blocks to all interactive components replacing box-shadow focus rings with outline: 2px solid Highlight; (2) Refactor hx-accordion-item to APG button-in-heading pattern; (3) Add keyboard alternative for hx-color-picker 2D gradient; (4) Remove duplicate aria-live from hx-carousel slide-viewport; (5) Replace hx-file-upload dropzone div with native button; (6) Add option count live region to hx-select; (7) Increase placeholder color token to neutral-500.

finding: Full bundle (shared chunks + index) totals ~295 KB gzip, which is 5.8x over the 50 KB budget; the budget appears to be measured against externalized Lit only via the esbuild analysis script, but the Vite dist includes all 80+ component shared chunks and the budget tracking gap is never surfaced in CI.
recommendation: Clarify in CI whether the 50 KB full-bundle gate is enforced on the Vite dist output or only on the esbuild analysis script; if the former, the library is in critical violation. Document which artifact the budget applies to and add an automated size-limit check against dist/index.js + shared chunks.

finding: Vite shared chunk hx-date-picker-Bh8410Sf.js is 7,407 bytes gzip, exceeding its 8,192 byte budget by 785 bytes on top of base Lit overhead, and the ariaLabel for each calendar day cell calls date.toLocaleDateString() inline per render with no memoization — on a 6-week grid that is up to 42 format calls per render.
recommendation: Cache the long-form day ariaLabel string alongside other day cell data in _getDaysInGrid() so it is computed once per grid rebuild rather than once per render cycle; or memoize via a Map keyed on ISO date + locale.

finding: hx-select gzip size is 6,330 bytes against a 6,144 byte budget, making it 186 bytes over. The override was declared in bundle-budgets.json but the component still exceeds that raised limit, which means CI budget gate would fail.
recommendation: Audit the hx-select styles file for removable specificity layers; consider hoisting the FOCUSABLE_SELECTORS string to module scope (same pattern as hx-dialog) to reduce per-instance string allocation, and verify floating-ui positioning logic is not being inlined unexpectedly.

finding: hx-nav-item shared chunk is 5,757 bytes gzip, 637 bytes over the 5,120 byte standard budget with no override declared in bundle-budgets.json.
recommendation: Add a justified override to bundle-budgets.json or reduce the component — audit hx-nav-item for inlined icon SVG markup or redundant CSS that can be extracted to CSS custom properties.

finding: hx-tree-item shared chunk is 5,819 bytes gzip, 699 bytes over the 5,120 byte standard budget with no override declared.
recommendation: Profile hx-tree-item for inlined SVG icons or redundant toggle/expand logic that could be moved to shared utilities; add a justified budget override if reduction is not feasible.

finding: hx-time-picker chunk is 5,775 bytes gzip, 655 bytes over standard budget; it does have a 6,144 override in bundle-budgets.json but the chunk gzip is measured under 6,144, so this is a near-limit warning.
recommendation: Monitor closely — the current size is within its override budget but only 369 bytes of headroom remains. Any new feature will bust the budget. Identify the largest CSS section via the bundle analysis script before adding further functionality.

finding: hx-form chunk is 5,753 bytes gzip (633 bytes over 5,120) with no override declared; hx-form uses an AdoptedStylesheetsController and inlines a large scoped CSS block (helixFormScopedCss) that is likely a significant portion of this cost.
recommendation: Declare a justified override in bundle-budgets.json or extract the scoped CSS into a shareable stylesheet that can be deduplicated across builds; evaluate whether the AdoptedStylesheetsController itself adds unnecessary overhead for a single-use component.

finding: hx-file-upload is 5,688 bytes gzip, 568 bytes over the standard budget; bundle-budgets.json grants a 6,144 override (so within its raised limit), but the component recently added a11y fixes that pushed it up from its 4.64 KB baseline.
recommendation: Confirm CI gates enforce the 6,144 override. If the component grows further with PHI or audit features, revisit whether file-list rendering could be lazy-loaded only after the first file drop rather than being included in initial parse.

finding: hx-carousel-item is 5,211 bytes gzip, 91 bytes over the 5,120 standard budget. The component itself is trivially simple (single slot, one property, minimal render), which suggests the styles file contains significant CSS or the document-token-adoption import is adding unshared overhead.
recommendation: Verify whether document-token-adoption is being included per-component chunk at the Vite level; if so, confirm it is always deduplicated into the shared chunk. 91 bytes over budget is very marginal and may vanish with minifier tuning.

finding: hx-data-table chunk is 5,241 bytes gzip, 121 bytes over the 5,120 standard budget despite extending LitElement directly rather than HelixElement, suggesting the JSON converter for the columns property and the large CSS block are the primary contributors.
recommendation: Add a justified override to bundle-budgets.json and document that the JSON column converter adds ~300 bytes; alternatively extract the converter to a shared utility that can be tree-shaken by consumers who pass typed arrays rather than JSON strings.

finding: hx-drawer chunk is 5,190 bytes gzip, 70 bytes over the 5,120 standard budget with no override; body-scroll-lock utility is a shared chunk but FOCUSABLE_SELECTORS is duplicated as module-scope constants in both hx-dialog and hx-drawer.
recommendation: The 70-byte overage is very marginal. Verify FOCUSABLE_SELECTORS is deduplicated by Vite's chunking strategy or extract it to a shared focusable-selectors utility module. Declare a budget override if reduction is not possible.

finding: hx-number-input chunk is 5,313 bytes gzip, 193 bytes over the standard budget; bundle-budgets.json grants a 6,144 override so this is within its limit. Long-press repeat key logic contributes complexity.
recommendation: Monitor headroom — 831 bytes remain before the override is breached. Document that the long-press timer and ElementInternals form association are the primary overhead drivers.

finding: sideEffects in package.json includes './dist/components/*/index.js' and './src/components/*/index.ts' as side-effectful, which means any bundler importing a single component from the barrel export will skip tree-shaking for all component index files; combined with the top-level barrel import in src/index.ts executing document-token-adoption.js at import time, the side-effect surface is wider than necessary.
recommendation: Narrow sideEffects to only './dist/utilities/document-token-adoption.js' and '**/*.css'. Component index files that only re-export named exports are pure and should not be listed as side-effectful.

finding: src/index.ts unconditionally executes import './utilities/document-token-adoption.js' at module evaluation time (not in a function), meaning any consumer who imports even a single named export from '@helixui/library' will trigger document.adoptedStyleSheets mutation as a side effect — even in SSR or test environments.
recommendation: The ensureDocumentTokens() function already has a SSR guard, but the bare import still causes the module to evaluate and attempt to read the Symbol.for key; wrap the auto-invocation with a typeof document guard or move auto-invocation to a separate side-effect-only entry point rather than the primary barrel.

finding: Each component individually re-imports document-token-adoption.js (100 files, 100 occurrences confirmed), resulting in 100 side-effectful import statements spread across the codebase. While Vite deduplicates this into a single shared chunk, esbuild-based consumer builds must also detect and deduplicate it.
recommendation: Since tokens are now adopted at the document level, the per-component import is redundant for any consumer that also imports the library barrel. Document this as intentional defensive coding and confirm the CI tree-shaking test verifies deduplication works correctly.

finding: preserveModules is not set in vite.config.ts; instead, code-splitting produces named shared chunks per component. While functional, this means consumers cannot reliably import a single component at a deterministic path without going through the per-component entry points.
recommendation: The per-component entry points in the exports map do provide deterministic paths. This is acceptable but should be explicitly documented as the canonical tree-shaking import path; the barrel import is only suitable for bundler-managed tree-shaking.

finding: 80 component files extend LitElement directly (bypassing HelixElement) while the remaining ~20 extend HelixElement. This inconsistency is not a tree-shaking issue per se but creates branching in the shared helix-element chunk that cannot be removed by tree-shaking even for components that only need LitElement.
recommendation: For purely presentational components with no form association (e.g. hx-carousel-item, hx-visually-hidden, hx-divider), extending LitElement directly is the correct and lighter choice. Document the decision rule: HelixElement only when form association or ElementInternals are required.

finding: _hueColor() and _previewColor() are plain private methods called directly in render() and _renderGrid()/_renderHueSlider()/_renderOpacitySlider() — each full re-render recomputes HSV-to-RGB conversion (hsvToRgb) and string formatting. During pointer drag events, this fires on every pointermove dispatching requestUpdate(), meaning color math runs at pointer-move frequency.
recommendation: Memoize _hueColor() and _previewColor() results as private instance fields computed only inside willUpdate() when _hsv changes; this avoids redundant computation during the render phase itself and reduces garbage pressure on frequently-updated strings.

finding: requestUpdate() is explicitly called inside _updateGridFromPointer(), _updateHueFromPointer(), and _updateOpacityFromPointer() after modifying _hsv (which is a @state), resulting in double-scheduling: assigning to a @state already schedules an update, and the additional requestUpdate() call is redundant.
recommendation: Remove the three explicit requestUpdate() calls from the drag handlers; the @state assignment on this._hsv is sufficient to schedule a Lit microtask update. The double scheduling currently causes no visible bug but wastes a scheduler round-trip on every pointermove.

finding: hx-date-picker uses updated() rather than willUpdate() to react to value and _isOpen changes, which means setFormValue, _updateValidity, and event listener attachment all run after the DOM has been updated and painted, adding a synchronous post-paint work unit.
recommendation: Move the setFormValue and _updateValidity calls from updated() to willUpdate(), which runs before the render and avoids an extra microtask. Only DOM-dependent side effects (focus management, event listeners that need the rendered calendar) legitimately belong in updated().

finding: _getDaysInGrid() is called directly in render() with no memoization. It allocates up to 42 Date objects per render plus the cells array. On every _focusedDay change (which is @state), the full grid is reconstructed.
recommendation: Move grid computation to willUpdate() and cache the result in a private field, invalidating only when _viewYear, _viewMonth, or value changes. This avoids reallocating 42 Date objects on every focus change.

finding: _renderDayGrid() creates inline arrow function click handlers for each day button via @click=${() => { this._selectDay(date); }}, which allocates a new closure per day per render. With 42 cells rendered each time any @state changes (including _focusedDay), this creates up to 42 closures per focus keystroke.
recommendation: Use a single delegated click handler at the grid level that reads data-day from the event target and dispatches to _selectDay, eliminating per-cell closure allocation. This is the same pattern already used in similar list-rendering components.

finding: Across 50 components, updated() is used; of these, hx-date-picker and hx-dialog set @state fields inside updated() (e.g. _liveMessage, _viewYear, _viewMonth), which triggers a second render cycle synchronously. While the guard conditions prevent infinite loops, the double-render pattern wastes a microtask.
recommendation: Prefer willUpdate() for all state synchronization that does not require reading from the rendered DOM; reserve updated() only for side effects that need the new DOM (focus management, third-party library calls, ResizeObserver registration).

finding: hx-combobox uses repeat() with correct key functions for the option list, which is good. However, the debounce implementation for filtering is not visible in the first 80 lines reviewed; if filter operations run synchronously on every keystroke without batching, long option lists will block the main thread.
recommendation: Verify that the filter step in hx-combobox uses a debounce or schedules filtering via requestAnimationFrame; if filtering is synchronous with large option sets, add a debounce with a 100-150ms delay matching the INP budget.

finding: hx-data-table uses repeat() for row rendering which is correct. However it extends LitElement directly rather than HelixElement and does not guard JSON parsing of the columns attribute behind willUpdate(); the converter runs on every attribute mutation regardless of whether columns actually changed.
recommendation: Move JSON parsing validation into willUpdate() behind a changedProperties.has('columns') guard to avoid redundant parse operations when other properties change.

finding: hx-nav uses repeat() with index as key rather than a stable item identifier (_item, i) => i, which means when items array is reordered, Lit cannot reuse DOM nodes — it treats every reordering as a full replacement.
recommendation: Use a stable key from the item itself (e.g. item.href or item.label) instead of the array index. Index-based keys are equivalent to no keys in terms of DOM reuse on reorder.

finding: guard() and cache() directives from lit/directives are not used anywhere in the component library (0 occurrences). For components with expensive sub-trees that rarely change — such as hx-color-picker's gradient grid SVG, hx-data-table's header row, and hx-date-picker's weekday header row — guard() would prevent unnecessary virtual DOM diffing.
recommendation: Add guard() around hx-date-picker's weekday headers (_renderWeekdayHeaders) which is locale-only dependent and never changes mid-session; add guard() around hx-color-picker's grid background when only the thumb position changes.

finding: hx-dialog calls querySelector('...') inside render() when deriving the trigger element for focus restoration: this.shadowRoot?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[part="trigger"]'). This pattern forces a DOM query on every render rather than using the @query decorator.
recommendation: Refactor the focus-target resolution to use a @query decorator or a cached private field populated in firstUpdated(); querySelector in render() is documented in the agent system prompt as an anti-pattern to avoid.

finding: The deprecated mergeTokenStyles() function remains exported in src/base/styles.ts with a @deprecated JSDoc tag but is still re-exported from src/index.ts, meaning tree-shakers that cannot eliminate re-exports will include it in every consumer build.
recommendation: Remove the mergeTokenStyles export from src/index.ts with a semver-appropriate deprecation timeline; the function's body is minimal but its presence in the public API prevents the associated module from being eliminated by bundlers.

finding: CSS custom property chains use three-tier var() nesting (primitive -> semantic -> component-level) across all component styles. While this is the correct design-token architecture, deep var() chains can cause recalculation cascades in browsers when a parent token changes, especially if the same token is read in many selectors.
recommendation: This pattern is architecturally correct. Ensure tokens are only read at the :host level via local private custom properties (--_bg: var(--hx-button-bg, var(--hx-color-primary-500))) and that inner selectors reference only the private alias, not the full chain — this minimizes style recalculation scope.

finding: hx-form uses Light DOM rendering (createRenderRoot returns this) and injects scoped CSS via AdoptedStylesheetsController, which writes to document.adoptedStyleSheets. The scoped CSS for a single form component competing with other document-level stylesheets increases selector specificity requirements and can cause layout recalculation when a form is first rendered.
recommendation: Audit helixFormScopedCss for any selectors that match broad document-level elements (e.g. input, label, select without component prefix) — these will affect all matching elements in the document, not just those inside hx-form. Scope all selectors to :is(hx-form *) or a unique class to prevent bleed.

finding: hx-color-picker's gradient grid uses styleMap() to set --_hue-color and --_thumb-x/--_thumb-y on inline styles during every drag event. This is correct (CSS custom properties on inline style trigger minimal recalc), but the --_preview-color is also computed in render() via _previewColor() and applied via styleMap, creating a pattern where three separate style computations run per render.
recommendation: Combine all dynamically-updated CSS custom properties into a single styleMap call on the host element or a single container, reducing the number of style attribute updates per render cycle from 3+ to 1.

finding: Zero production dependencies beyond Lit core and workspace tokens are present in the library's dependencies field — @floating-ui/dom is correctly listed as a peerDependency, preventing it from being bundled. This is excellent dependency hygiene.
recommendation: Maintain this constraint strictly. Any future utility (date formatting, color parsing beyond the internal color-utils.ts, validation) must remain internal or be gated as a peerDependency. The current zero-deps policy is a competitive advantage.

finding: color-utils.ts is an internal module implementing full HSV/RGB/HSL/HEX color math without pulling in any external color library — this is the correct approach for keeping bundle size within the 8KB override budget. The entire color math adds approximately 1-1.5KB gzip.
recommendation: No action needed. Document explicitly in bundle-budgets.json that the color-utils.ts is the intentional internal replacement for external color libraries like chroma.js or tinycolor2.

finding: No IntersectionObserver-based lazy registration patterns exist anywhere in the library codebase. Heavy components (hx-color-picker 6.97 KB, hx-date-picker 7.4 KB, hx-combobox 6.9 KB, hx-data-table, hx-form) are registered eagerly via @customElement decorator at import time — there is no mechanism for deferring their registration until first use.
recommendation: Provide documented lazy-loading examples in the Drupal integration docs showing IntersectionObserver-based dynamic import() for hx-color-picker, hx-date-picker, and hx-combobox. These three components alone account for ~21 KB gzip and are typically used on specific form pages rather than site-wide. No source changes required — documentation and Drupal behavior examples are the deliverable.

finding: The CDN build strategy documented in build-cdn.mjs produces a Strategy A (full bundle ~816 KB raw) that loads all 80+ components synchronously, which is the primary Drupal delivery mechanism. No lazy-loading documentation exists for the CDN path; all components load regardless of whether the current Drupal page uses any of them.
recommendation: Publish a Drupal-specific lazy-loading pattern using the Strategy B split bundle output (per-component CDN files) paired with IntersectionObserver or Drupal behaviors; add this to the Drupal integration docs. The split bundle output already exists in dist/cdn/components/.

finding: hx-dialog, hx-drawer, hx-color-picker, and hx-date-picker are modal/overlay components that are universally off-screen on page load — they are ideal IntersectionObserver candidates but all four are included in the CDN full bundle without any lazy-loading infrastructure.
recommendation: Add a documented withLazyRegistration() helper or a separate lazy entry point (e.g. @helixui/library/components/hx-dialog/lazy) that uses dynamic import() gated on IntersectionObserver intersection; this pattern would defer 4 of the 5 heaviest components until needed.

finding: hx-carousel and hx-carousel-item are typically used below-the-fold on content pages and would benefit from lazy registration, but the carousel-item chunk is already over budget (5,211 bytes) and both components are registered at import time with no deferred-import path.
recommendation: Document hx-carousel as a lazy-load candidate in the performance guide; provide an IntersectionObserver pattern specifically for carousel since images inside typically are the LCP candidate and delaying carousel JS registration can meaningfully improve LCP.

finding: The bundle-analysis.js script documents the IntersectionObserver lazy-loading pattern in its recommendations section (intersection-observer-lazy), but this is only visible in the audit JSON output — no equivalent documentation, code example, or Drupal behavior file is published for consumers.
recommendation: Surface the lazy-loading pattern from bundle-analysis.js recommendations into the public Astro Starlight docs and the Drupal CDN integration guide; add a concrete code example for hx-color-picker and hx-date-picker.

finding: hx-button uses classMap() and ifDefined() directives correctly. The loading state conditionally renders a spinner SVG using the nothing sentinel, which is the correct Lit pattern for conditional rendering.
recommendation: No action needed. hx-button is a well-optimized Lit component — @query is used for DOM references, willUpdate() handles property synchronization, and nothing is used for conditional sections.

finding: hx-select uses repeat() with (opt) => opt.value as the key function, which is correct. However the dropdown listbox is conditionally rendered on _open state — while correct for reducing DOM, this means every open/close cycle fully destroys and recreates the listbox DOM including ARIA attributes, which may cause flicker in screen readers.
recommendation: Consider using Lit's cache() directive or a CSS visibility pattern for the listbox to preserve ARIA live region state across open/close cycles; this trades a small constant DOM cost for improved AT continuity.

finding: hx-pagination uses repeat() for page number rendering with stable keys ('ellipsis-N' or 'page-N'), which correctly enables DOM reuse when paginating through large datasets.
recommendation: No action needed. Pagination render optimization is correct. Verify that the repeat key includes both page number and ellipsis type to prevent DOM identity confusion when ellipsis positions shift.

finding: hx-file-upload uses repeat() for file list rendering with (entry) => entry.file.name + entry.file.size as the key, which is a good approximation but could collide for files with identical names and sizes. More importantly, the progress state updates for individual files will cause repeat() to reconcile the entire list on every progress tick.
recommendation: Add a stable unique ID to each file entry at upload time (e.g. a monotonically incrementing index or crypto.randomUUID()) and use that as the repeat key; this eliminates any key collision risk and makes DOM reconciliation O(1) per file rather than O(n).

finding: hx-time-picker uses repeat() for time slot rendering with (slot) => slot.value as the key, and the slot list is only rendered when _open is true — this is good. However the slot list appears to be rebuilt on every open rather than being memoized, meaning potentially hundreds of time option objects are reallocated per open.
recommendation: Compute the time slots array once in connectedCallback() or the first time the picker opens and cache it; time slots are deterministic from the step property and do not need recomputation on each open unless step changes.

finding: The aria-delegation mixin (mixinDelegatesAria) used by hx-button intercepts all 40+ ARIA attributes via observedAttributes and re-dispatches them to the inner button element. This means every ARIA attribute set on the host element triggers attributeChangedCallback, a property access, and an attribute set on the inner element — three DOM operations instead of one.
recommendation: Profile whether the aria-delegation overhead is measurable for interactive components like hx-button used in high-frequency scenarios (data tables with hundreds of buttons). If overhead is measurable, consider limiting the intercepted attribute list to only those actually needed by each component rather than all 40+ ARIA attributes uniformly.

finding: hx-counter implements animated number counting, which by definition involves rapid @state updates driving re-renders at animation frame rate. The component calls requestUpdate() in the animation loop — it is unclear if this is guarded by willUpdate() to batch updates or if each increment triggers a full Lit update cycle.
recommendation: Verify the counter animation uses requestAnimationFrame and batches state updates; if _currentValue is a @state that is incremented per frame, consider using this.requestUpdate() only and updating a non-reactive private field directly, then triggering a single render at the end of each frame via requestAnimationFrame.

finding: Per-component entry points are correctly implemented via auto-discovery in vite.config.ts (discoverEntryPoints()), covering all hx-* component directories and exposing each as a named Rollup entry. The exports map in package.json correctly surfaces './components/*' paths.

Vite build uses minify: 'esbuild' which is the fastest and produces competitive output size. All Lit packages and @helixui/tokens and @floating-ui are correctly externalized via the external regex patterns, preventing any accidental bundling of the Lit runtime into component chunks.

Shared utilities (body-scroll-lock, id-counter, helix-element, document-token-adoption, aria-delegation, FormMixin) are correctly extracted into named shared chunks by Vite's code-splitting, preventing duplication across component chunks. The 14 shared chunks confirm effective deduplication.

devWarn utility correctly uses import.meta.env.DEV which is statically replaced at build time by Vite, meaning all devWarn calls are eliminated from production builds as dead code. This is the correct tree-shaking pattern for development-only utilities.

body-scroll-lock is implemented as a 58-line internal utility with a reference-counted stack pattern, avoiding any external lock library dependency. The module-level state (_lockCount, _savedOverflow) is correctly handled to prevent race conditions between multiple overlays.

hx-date-picker correctly memoizes Intl.DateTimeFormat instances (_weekdayFormatter, _monthFormatter, _cachedWeekdayNames) and rebuilds them only when locale changes via _ensureFormatters(). This is a good optimization for a component that renders 7 weekday headers and a month name on every calendar open.
recommendation: No action needed on the formatter memoization. Consider also memoizing the full-form day ariaLabel format (noted separately under render-performance) using the same locale-keyed pattern.

finding: @query decorator is consistently used across components for DOM element references (hx-color-picker, hx-date-picker, hx-combobox, hx-text-input all use @query), correctly avoiding querySelector calls in the render path.

hx-color-picker correctly caches bounding rect at pointerdown (_dragRect) rather than reading getBoundingClientRect() on every pointermove event. This is a significant render-performance optimization that avoids forced synchronous layout on every drag frame.

Shadow DOM encapsulation is used consistently across all components. The document-token-adoption adopted-stylesheet pattern correctly provides CSS custom property inheritance through Shadow DOM boundaries without per-component token redeclaration, which is the optimal architecture for a Lit component library.
Vitest browser mode is correctly configured with Playwright Chromium, headless, 1280x720 viewport, and 30s test timeout — exactly matching enterprise Shadow DOM requirements.
Coverage provider is v8 with appropriate exclusions for styles, stories, and index re-exports, but coverage is disabled by default in CI — only enabled via pnpm run test:coverage.
recommendation: Consider enabling a lightweight coverage pass in CI on changed components only; the current smart-test script already scopes to changed components and the overhead would be minimal.

finding: coverage-config.json lists 95% threshold as the target but shows 76 out of ~80 components as explicitly exempted, meaning the coverage gate is effectively unenforced for nearly the entire library.
recommendation: Establish a rolling remediation schedule: remove no more than 5 exemptions per sprint rather than bulk-exempting the entire library; bind each exemption removal to a completed qa-engineer-automation feature ticket.

finding: Global afterEach(cleanup) pattern is consistent across all test files examined; fixtureContainer.innerHTML = '' correctly resets DOM state between tests without leaving orphaned custom elements.
test-utils.ts correctly exports fixture, shadowQuery, shadowQueryAll, oneEvent, cleanup, and checkA11y (axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA) — the full canonical utility set for Shadow DOM testing.
recommendation: The fixture() function does not recursively wait for nested updateComplete on child custom elements; add a helper like waitForAll() that accepts a host and resolves all slotted child updateCompletes for composite tests.

finding: The vitest.config.ts include pattern covers src/components/**/*.test.ts but the hx-style-scope test lives in src/components/hx-style-scope/__tests__/ — this is an inconsistent convention that could cause future tests to be silently excluded if placed in a __tests__ subdirectory that doesn't match the pattern.
recommendation: Normalize: either always place component tests at hx-foo/hx-foo.test.ts or document the __tests__ pattern as the official convention; update the include glob to explicitly cover both.

finding: hx-menu.test.ts provides comprehensive coverage of hx-menu, hx-menu-item, and hx-menu-divider in a single file with 842 lines covering rendering, events, keyboard navigation, roving tabindex, public methods, typeahead, submenu ARIA, and axe-core audits.
All three custom elements in the hx-menu directory (hx-menu, hx-menu-item, hx-menu-divider) are tested in the consolidated test file with dedicated describe blocks.
Six axe-core test scenarios cover hx-menu with labels, disabled items, checkbox/radio menu items, and hx-menu-divider — all using checkA11y() with full WCAG 2.1 AA ruleset.
Disabled item suppression, loading state event blocking, radio mutual-exclusion, multi-character typeahead buffer, and roving tabindex updates are all exercised.
recommendation: Add a test for hx-menu rendered with zero items (empty menu) to verify focusFirst/focusLast do not throw.

finding: hx-data-table.test.ts is one of the most complete test files in the library — 1143 lines covering rendering, sorting, row selection, row click, empty state, loading state, pagination, keyboard navigation, JSON coercion, CSS parts, i18n, and dynamic data updates.

Edge cases include invalid JSON attribute recovery, sparse rows array, ArrowLeft at first cell boundary, ArrowRight at last cell boundary, single-column table keyboard nav, and cell cache invalidation on rows change.
recommendation: Add coverage for column resize interactions mentioned in coverage-config.json exemption as a known gap.

finding: axe-core audits cover default state, selectable, loading, and empty state; aria-sort ascending/descending/none, aria-selected, aria-busy, role=grid, and tabindex for grid keyboard navigation are all explicitly asserted.

hx-carousel.test.ts covers rendering, ARIA, navigation, loop, autoplay (including prefers-reduced-motion, pause-on-mouseenter, disconnectedCallback cleanup), keyboard, touch swipe (vertical and horizontal), focus management, and axe-core.
hx-carousel-item is tested only compositionally within hx-carousel tests; there is no isolated describe block for hx-carousel-item properties or ARIA contributions.
recommendation: Add a dedicated describe('hx-carousel-item') block testing its role, aria-roledescription, and visibility state changes in isolation.

finding: coverage-config.json notes touch/swipe gesture handling and autoplay interval logic need more coverage; touch swipe tests exist but pointer-based drag (PointerEvent) is not tested, and autoplay resume-on-mouseleave is missing.
recommendation: Add PointerEvent-based swipe simulation and a test that autoplay resumes when mouse leaves the carousel after a mouseenter pause.

finding: hx-nav.test.ts contains 887 lines covering rendering, JSON items converter, label, orientation, links/active state, URL sanitization (javascript: and data: protocol blocking), submenus, mobile toggle, events, keyboard navigation, focusout/outside-click collapse, and i18n overrides.
Three axe-core tests cover horizontal, vertical, and submenu-open states; aria-current, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-label, and aria-labelledby are all explicitly verified.
recommendation: Add a test that nav-item link has no aria-haspopup when it is a leaf link (current implementation verifies the negative on submenu triggers but not leaf links explicitly).

finding: Keyboard navigation tests use vi.spyOn to verify focus() is called on the correct element rather than checking document.activeElement through shadow boundaries, which is a pragmatic pattern for Lit's delegatesFocus complexity.
recommendation: Where feasible, prefer checking el.shadowRoot.activeElement over focus spies for stronger assertions about which element actually received focus.

finding: coverage-config.json reports hx-button at 64% lines and 50% branches; the test file exists with variant/size/type rendering tests but form-associated integration (formAssociated=true), loading state interaction blocking, and href-link rendering paths are insufficiently covered.
recommendation: Add tests for: button type=submit triggering form submission, loading=true blocking hx-click, href rendering as anchor-like element, and formAction/formMethod attribute reflection.

finding: The button test file lacks axe-core checkA11y() calls; aria-disabled, aria-busy (loading), and aria-label for icon-only buttons are not verified by automated accessibility assertions.
recommendation: Add axe-core tests for disabled state, loading state, and a variant with icon-only content (requiring aria-label).

finding: coverage-config.json classifies hx-accordion as skeleton-only; the test file has 70 tests but coverage is reported below threshold — hx-accordion-item sub-component has a separate describe block but complex animation and focusout-close paths are not covered.
recommendation: Expand to test animation state transitions (is-animating attribute), focusout-triggered collapse, allowMultiple=false enforcement when multiple items are initially expanded, and hx-accordion-item in isolation.

finding: coverage-config.json marks hx-tabs as skeleton-only despite having 76 tests; hx-tab-panel and hx-tab sub-element isolation testing, ARIA tabpanel relationships, and keyboard navigation edge cases (wrapping, disabled tab skipping) need expansion.
recommendation: Add tests for: tab panel hidden attribute toggling, aria-controls/aria-labelledby linkage between tab and panel, disabled tab keyboard skip, and tab panel slot content rendering.

finding: coverage-config.json notes SSR browser API guards bring coverage below threshold; dialog focus trap behavior, Escape key dismiss, and backdrop click dismiss are the most critical untested paths for a modal component.
recommendation: Prioritize focus trap testing (Tab key cycles within dialog, focus returns to trigger on close), Escape key dismiss, backdrop click dismiss, and scroll lock/restore.

finding: Dialog has no axe-core test in the test file for its open state; aria-modal, aria-labelledby, and focus management after open/close are critical accessibility requirements for a modal component that are unverified.
recommendation: Add axe-core checkA11y() tests for: dialog in open state, dialog with aria-labelledby pointing to title slot, and focus restoration on close.

finding: coverage-config.json marks hx-text-input as skeleton-only despite it being a form-associated component (formAssociated=true); ElementInternals setFormValue, constraint validation (required, pattern, minLength), and form reset/restore callbacks are not covered.
recommendation: Add form integration tests: place hx-text-input inside a <form>, submit it, verify FormData value; test required validation reporting, pattern mismatch, and form.reset() clearing the value.

finding: No axe-core checkA11y() calls exist in hx-text-input.test.ts; aria-invalid on validation failure, aria-describedby pointing to help-text, and aria-required are not verified.
recommendation: Add axe-core tests for: valid state, required + empty (aria-invalid=true), and with help-text (aria-describedby wiring).

finding: coverage-config.json reports hx-select below threshold due to SSR guards; as a form-associated component, setFormValue syncing, constraint validation, and keyboard navigation of the options list are the key uncovered paths.
recommendation: Add tests for: option selection updating FormData, keyboard Arrow navigation through options, Enter to confirm selection, Escape to close without selection, and aria-activedescendant updates.

finding: coverage-config.json marks hx-checkbox as skeleton-only; as a form-associated component with indeterminate state, neither the indeterminate visual state, ElementInternals form participation, nor keyboard Enter/Space activation are verified.
recommendation: Add tests for: indeterminate state rendering, Space key toggling checked state, setFormValue with checked/unchecked values, and constraint validation with required attribute.

finding: No aria-checked, aria-required, or aria-invalid assertions exist for hx-checkbox; no axe-core tests are present.
recommendation: Add axe-core tests for: unchecked, checked, indeterminate, required, and disabled states; explicitly assert aria-checked on the shadow DOM input or role=checkbox element.

finding: hx-radio-group has a separate hx-radio.test.ts file for the sub-element but coverage-config.json marks radio-group as skeleton-only; hx-radio sub-element form participation, arrow key selection, and roving tabindex are the key gaps.
recommendation: Expand hx-radio.test.ts to cover: Arrow key focus movement between radios, Enter/Space selection, aria-checked state toggling, formAssociated value reporting, and required validation.

finding: hx-radio has its own test file (hx-radio.test.ts) which is a good pattern, but coverage-config.json indicates the group's validation state propagation and error describedby wiring are not tested.
recommendation: Add integration tests in hx-radio-group.test.ts that verify the group's error message is linked to all child radios via aria-describedby.

finding: coverage-config.json marks hx-switch as skeleton-only; as a form-associated component, setFormValue, checked/unchecked value submission, and Space key activation are not verified.
recommendation: Add tests: Space key toggles checked, form submission includes switch value when checked, submission excludes value when unchecked, and aria-checked reflects state.

finding: coverage-config.json notes SSR browser API guards; textarea as a form-associated component needs form integration tests for setFormValue, minLength/maxLength constraint validation, and auto-resize behavior testing.
recommendation: Add tests for: auto-resize (rows increasing as content grows), maxLength enforcement, setFormValue syncing to FormData, and required validation on empty value.

finding: coverage-config.json flagged hx-number-input as 0% lines; as a form-associated component it requires stepper increment/decrement button tests, min/max clamping, and keyboard Arrow key value changes.
recommendation: Add tests: increment/decrement buttons change value, ArrowUp/ArrowDown keyboard increment, min/max boundaries clamp value, step attribute controls increment size, and setFormValue syncs to FormData.

finding: coverage-config.json notes SSR guards; slider is form-associated and requires ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End keyboard value change tests, min/max/step attribute enforcement, and setFormValue integration.
recommendation: Add tests: Arrow keys adjust value by step, Home/End jump to min/max, pointer drag simulation (PointerEvent), and form submission includes slider value.

finding: coverage-config.json marks hx-combobox as skeleton-only; as a form-associated composite widget with ARIA combobox pattern (role=combobox, aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant, aria-controls), the coverage gap is critical for healthcare accessibility compliance.
recommendation: Treat hx-combobox as P0 for test expansion: cover open/close state, option keyboard navigation, Enter to select, Escape to close, filtered results, aria-activedescendant updates, and form value submission.

finding: coverage-config.json notes calendar grid keyboard navigation and locale-specific edge cases are unaddressed; hx-date-picker is form-associated and must work correctly in healthcare date-of-birth and appointment scheduling contexts.
recommendation: Add tests: calendar grid Arrow key navigation, Page Up/Down month navigation, Home/End in week row, invalid date input handling, locale formatting verification, and setFormValue with ISO date string.

finding: No axe-core tests exist for hx-date-picker open/closed states; the calendar grid requires specific ARIA grid roles, aria-label on day cells, and aria-selected for chosen date — none of which are currently verified.
recommendation: Add axe-core tests for: picker closed state, picker open state with calendar grid, selected date state, and disabled dates.

finding: coverage-config.json notes time parsing edge cases and AM/PM toggle interactions need coverage; as a form-associated component used in healthcare scheduling, 12-hour/24-hour parsing and invalid time input recovery are critical paths.
recommendation: Add tests: AM/PM toggle changes hour value, 24-hour format parsing, invalid time string falls back gracefully, Arrow key hour/minute increment, and setFormValue with time string.

finding: coverage-config.json notes drag-and-drop and file validation paths require browser File API infrastructure not yet in place; hx-file-upload is form-associated and critical for healthcare document workflows.
recommendation: Use vitest browser mode DataTransfer API mock to simulate file drop; test accept attribute filtering, maxSize validation rejection, multiple=false single-file enforcement, and hx-file-change event payload.

finding: coverage-config.json notes recursive tree rendering and deep keyboard traversal are coverage gaps; hx-tree-view has 83 tests but nested node expand/collapse state management and ArrowRight to expand / ArrowLeft to collapse patterns need verification.
